_purpose: The declared palette for W3, for palette_gate.py. A specification names materials; this states what colours those materials can legally occupy, so 'the twin contains something not in the spec' becomes measurable instead of a matter of noticing.
_why_this_exists: Arm B's view 6 came back with a navy blue sleeve on a tunic the specification calls SLEEVELESS. Seven views measured exactly 0 px of blue; view 6 measured 5,590 px, 6.17% of its figure, 4,882 of them in one connected blob. Nothing in the route would have caught it before projection — it would have been painted onto the mesh and found later, or not at all. This is the defect class E07 established the old metrics are blind to: a large region of the WRONG MATERIAL, smooth inside itself, contributing only its rim to any high-pass statistic.
_bands_are_declared_from_the_SPEC_not_me: Deriving the allowed bands from the clean twins would be circular — they would pass by construction. These come from the sixteen named materials in E08-spec-prompt.json, and are then CHECKED against the measured region colours in E08-contradiction-dE.json (the SPEC arm), which is a different image than the ones being gated.
_the_chroma_floor_is_load_bearing: Neutral colour has no meaningful hue — the angle is noise at low chroma, the same fact that made the contradiction test's Dh column unreadable on collapsed rows. W3's steel blade measures C* 1.6-2.8 at hue 266-268, which sits squarely in the BLUE band. Without a chroma floor the gate would flag the greatsword on every view. Anything at or below min_chroma is unconstrained.

allowed_bands.name: warm
allowed_bands.covers: red beard, dark red skirt, gold pauldrons/medallion/knees/crossguard/pommel, brown leather belt and bracers, skin
allowed_bands.measured_examples: beard h46.6 | skirt h19.8 | pauldron h79.3 | medallion h79.4 | belt h87.6 | bracer h53.4 | scalp h48.3

allowed_bands.name: green
allowed_bands.covers: dark green knitted tunic, green cloth panels in the skirt
allowed_bands._margin_note: the skirt panels sit at 141.6, so the lower edge is set at 125 rather than 130 to leave room; the band is not tight around a single measurement.

_forbidden_by_construction: 105-125 (yellow-green) and 210-360 (cyan, blue, violet, magenta) at any chroma above the floor. The blue sleeve measured hue 240-320.
_what_this_gate_CANNOT_do: It tests COLOUR, not placement. Gold on the boots would pass every band while being flatly wrong, and a correctly-coloured element in the wrong location is invisible to it. It is a palette gate, not a specification gate — it catches material that is not in the spec at all, which is exactly and only the failure it was built from. Do not let a green light here be read as 'the twin matches the spec'.

gate._why_two_thresholds: One garment and scattered speckle are different failures and a single total conflates them. View 6 was 6.17% with a 4,882 px blob; a rim of antialiasing at a material boundary would be a similar total spread over hundreds of tiny components. The blob bound is the one that catches an invented garment.
gate._thresholds_are_stated_before_the_re-rol: Set from the seven clean views measuring exactly 0 px, so any non-zero result is already outside the observed distribution. 0.5% and 800 px are an order of magnitude above nothing and an order of magnitude below the failure. Not tuned to let anything through.
gate.⚠_max_offpalette_pct_WITHDRAWN: Ruled 2026-08-04 (fc9a2e2), after it failed both re-rolls that the blob bound cleared. TWO independent reasons, and it is WITHDRAWN rather than re-derived — withdrawing is not choosing a new number, which is the move that would be forbidden.
gate._reason_1_its_stated_derivation_does_not: The line above claims it was set from 'seven clean views measuring exactly 0 px' and is 'an order of magnitude above nothing'. That 0 px came from an ad-hoc BLUE-ONLY check, not from this gate. This gate's clean baseline is 0.06%-0.33%, so 0.5% was 1.5x the highest clean view. A condition whose stated derivation does not describe it never had a valid derivation — it is not a tight threshold, it is not a threshold. Same disposition as project_twins' `assert seen.mean() > 0.30`, E07's <=3.25, and the stratum area-loss gate.
gate._reason_2_the_denominator_moves_with_the: Figure area swings 1.65x between a profile (90,553 px) and a rear three-quarter (149,780 px), while off-palette pixels are a BOUNDARY phenomenon scaling with perimeter. twin_6's 603 px sits beside the passing views' 462 and 401 and failed only on geometry. Fourth moving denominator in this repo.
gate._what_is_lost_named_rather_than_glossed: The SPECKLE half of the gate goes with it. Distributed off-palette contamination is now unbounded, and twin_2 projected carrying 1,073 px — ~2.3x the passing views in ABSOLUTE terms with only a 402 px blob, so the excess is diffuse. That is recorded as uncharacterised, and Gate 1 judges it.
gate._replacement_is_specified_as_a_UNIT_not_: Normalise by PERIMETER, or report absolute count with figure area beside it. Its threshold must be derived from a clean baseline measured BEFORE the arm that tests it. DO NOT BUILD IT WHILE LOOKING AT RESULTS IT WOULD JUDGE — that is exactly how the withdrawn one went wrong.
